author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human — workspace-architectural decision. Both race issues in this bead are unfixable inside the current ChatBackend trait shape: lost increment + stale-read overwrite both require an atomic transaction across the SpaceInvite uses write AND the Space members write, which the trait does not provide.

Options considered:

(a) Add ChatBackend::redeem_space_invite(&self, caller, account_id, space_id, invite_id, new_member: SpaceMember) -> Result<(u64 /* new_uses */, Space /* updated members */), BackendSetError>. The backend performs both writes inside one atomic operation (transaction, lock, CAS, whatever the storage layer offers). handle_space_join calls this single method on the invite path.

(b) Extend update_object semantics with a compare-and-swap primitive — "update SpaceInvite with expected_uses=5, new_uses=6; reject if uses changed." Caller retries on conflict. This would generalise to other backend types but adds CAS semantics to a method that downstream consumers do not need for most object types.

(c) Wrap both writes in a single ChatBackend::apply_join_invite call with two-phase logic — but the two writes target two different JmapObject types (SpaceInvite and Space), which apply_space_patch is not shaped for.

Recommendation: Path (a). Reasons:

1. The wire format stays unchanged (single Space/join method with optional inviteCode).

2. The atomicity is pushed to the layer that can implement it — the backend has direct knowledge of its storage primitives (transaction, optimistic concurrency control, distributed lock). The trait surface does NOT need to expose CAS semantics to every consumer.

3. Production backends can implement this against their native storage primitives (PG transaction, FoundationDB transaction, RocksDB write batch). The reference MemoryBackend implements it under a single mutex acquisition — already the existing atomicity model.

4. The current code in handle_space_join (TOCTOU re-read, recovery logic for race-loss) is a workaround for the missing atomicity primitive. With redeem_space_invite, ~80 lines of handler complexity collapse to a single call.

Cost of Path (a): 1 new trait method, MemoryBackend impl, default impl returning a "not supported" error so backends MUST override (or wire the legacy two-write path under a deprecation note).

Entanglement: JMAP-x2gd.10 (Space/join invite lookup is account-scoped; spec semantics are global) proposes essentially the same trait method — redeem_invite_code(code) -> (account_id, space_id, invite_id). The right signature is probably the union: redeem_space_invite_by_code(caller, code, new_member) -> Result<(account_id, space_id, uses, Space), BackendSetError>. .2 and .10 should be done together.

Further entanglement: this bead is also in the same family as .3 and .4 (permission-gating typed trait methods for SpaceInvite and SpaceBan). All four are arguing for typed methods on ChatBackend to replace the type-erased create_object<O> / update_object<O> generic path for object types whose mutations have spec-mandated semantics the generic path cannot express. Resolving the .3 / .4 architecture call (also human-labeled) probably wants to be done together with .2 / .10.

Filed as human-labeled rather than picking Path (a) unilaterally because (i) the choice between (a) / (b) / (c) is a workspace-architectural one that lands a new ChatBackend trait method default impl, (ii) it entangles with at least three other human-needing beads (.10, and indirectly .3 and .4), and (iii) downstream consumers (kith, stoa) that implement ChatBackend will need to provide this method.
